Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Short retention window: keystore exception action items & exec sync

Thanks Cynthia — copying product & ops so we can map owners. Quick summary and asks:

Context: Novamed/Helix are requesting a temporary (7-day) short retention window for a pilot that must be exempted from our standard 30-day ephemeral retention. This drives two compliance asks: evidence of audit log export for the window and a keystore (BYOK) flow clarification for key custody.

Action items I need help with before Friday EOD:
1) Ben: produce a sanitized sample export (audit logs + key IDs) for the 7-day window. Redact PII; keep key IDs and event timestamps. Deliverable: S3 export stub + README.
2) Karthik: confirm the recommended keystore flow for temporary CMKs — can we support a customer-managed CMK (bring-your-own) for a 7-day timeframe, and if so, what rotation/rollback steps do we enforce?
3) Marissa: product gating — list any runtime changes required for short-window mode (cache eviction, KV clear) and impacts on SLOs.
4) Grace: coordinate a 30-minute exec sync on Thu with Security + Sales + Ops to cover any SLA/credit asks.

Notes: we should treat this as an exception path (no code changes if possible) and prefer operational runbooks. If we need code-level fixes, escalate to the next sprint.

Proposed exec sync: Thu 08/06 10:00 PT — does this work?

Thanks,
Sofia
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 11:04 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks Cynthia — copying product & ops so we can map owners. Quick summary and asks:

I've prepared a sanitized sample export and a short README describing the fields and redaction steps. Key points:
- Export includes event_time (ISO), event_type, key_id (hashed), request_id, model_id, and retention_window_tag
- No payloads or user prompt text included; we replace prompt_text with a length indicator to show presence/absence
- Hashing approach: we salt key_id and persist mapping in a one-off, audited vault for the reviewer session only

Deliverables attached: short-window-ma-action-plan.xlsx (tab: export-sample) and keystore-flow.png showing the proof-of-concept flow where the customer supplies a short-lived CMK via KMS Import.

Open questions for Karthik: if we accept an imported CMK with a 7-day TTL, how do we signal revocation and prove key destruction to the auditor?

Ben
Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: short-window-ma-action-plan.xlsx, keystore-flow.png
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Cynthia Perez <cynthia.perez@helixbio.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short retention window: keystore exception action items & exec sync

Thanks all — summary from the technical side and next steps (from today's exec sync):

- Keystore approach: we can support a customer-provided short-lived CMK using our importable key wrapper pattern. For a 7-day window: the CMK is wrapped by an internal wrapping key; the import operation is recorded in our audit log.
- Revocation proof: we will perform a deterministic zeroize operation and publish a signed revocation artifact (timestamped hash of destroyed key material) into the auditor-only S3 bucket. That artifact + the salted key_id mapping (Ben's approach) should satisfy proof-of-destruction requirements.
- Operational constraints: this remains an exceptional flow. We need a runbook to: import CMK -> tag tenant resources -> export audit snapshot -> zeroize on TTL expiry -> generate revocation artifact. Marissa to confirm any product toggles; if none, Ops can run the manual runbook for pilot.

Deliverables by Mon 08/10:
- Ben: upload sanitized export to shared drive and hand off README (done, link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cEXAMPLE-ShortWindow).
- Karthik: publish runbook draft and revocation artifact template (JIRA:SEC-231).
- Marissa: confirm product gating overhead and sign-off for pilot.
- Grace: run pilot intake and sign off on customer-facing timeline.

Cynthia: can you confirm if the signed revocation artifact + sanitized export align with Novamed's audit requirements? If yes, we'll proceed with the pilot and treat this as an exception path.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
